source_of_truth: Read by hand in a Next.js App Router app. src/features/billing/invoiceToken.ts begins with `import 'server-only'`, so the module (and the INVOICE_SIGNING_SECRET it reads) must never be bundled for the browser. src/features/billing/InvoiceBadge.tsx declares 'use client' and statically imports { signInvoice } from './invoiceToken'. A 'use client' module that imports a 'server-only' module pulls server-only code into the client bundle; Next's build rejects it. The import is explicit and static (a verified runtime edge), so confirmed is the correct level.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

expected.rationale: A 'use client' component statically imports a module marked 'server-only'; this is exactly the boundary the marker forbids and Next fails the build on it. The edge is an explicit import (verified), so confirmed is the honest level.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: page.tsx is a Server Component (no 'use client'); it may import the client component, and it never imports the server-only module, so no boundary is crossed here.
